title: Automated Provenance and Evidence‑Scoring Judge for LLM Assertions in NetOps (Detecting 'No Issue' Hallucinations)
research_question: Can an automated provenance-scoring judge reliably distinguish supported 'no issue' / 'reachability holds' assertions from hallucinated assertions in LLM-generated NetOps diagnoses using purely programmatic (non-human) ground truth and deterministic provenance signals?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A provenance+evidence-scoring judge that combines deterministic retrieval grounding, syntactic/semantic validators, and telemetry cross-checks reduces unsupported 'no-issue' assertions compared to the LLM-alone baseline (measured by F1 on the unsupported/no-issue class).

The judge's binary decision (supported vs unsupported) achieves operationally usable precision/recall trade-offs (predefined thresholds) when tuned on a deterministic, programmatically labeled validation set.
exploratory_questions: Which provenance signal (retrieval evidence score, validator pass/fail, telemetry feature) contributes most to judge performance (ablation)?
How sensitive is judge performance to partial absence of retrieval or telemetry signals (deterministic sensitivity analysis)?
How do different deterministic prompt templates affect LLM propensity to produce unsupported 'no-issue' assertions?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic/high-fidelity emulator scenarios (publicly scripted topologies and deterministic traffic/telemetry generators) only; claims are explicitly bounded to these synthetic/emulated scenarios.
Reachability and simple health-check diagnostics (ICMP/forwarding, interface admin/down) as operational properties.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API instance (hosted_model_api_available per capability manifest). Exact model identifier will be recorded and published in execution logs and artifacts; preregistration fixes use of one hosted LLM instance for all experiment runs to preserve paired comparisons.
transformation_scope: Prompt templates (two fixed templates), retrieval embedding/indexing pipeline, deterministic index-build scripts, feature extraction transformations from telemetry and validator outputs, and the judge's feature vector construction.
primary_estimand: F1 score for the judge on the binary task of labeling an LLM assertion as 'supported' vs 'unsupported' for 'no-issue'/'reachability-holds' claims, evaluated on a held-out test split.
secondary_estimands: Precision and recall (supported/unsupported class) with 95% bootstrap CIs.
Difference in misclassification counts (discordant pairs) between judge and baseline (LLM-self-certainty or simple retrieval-threshold) assessed with McNemar's test.
Calibration (reliability) of judge confidence scores (Brier score / calibration curve).
sampling_plan: Construct 300 deterministic, scripted simulated network scenarios using public emulator images and deterministic traffic/telemetry generators (scripts published). For each scenario generate two LLM prompts (reachability-check and health-check) using two fixed prompt templates to produce 600 LLM outputs. Split outputs deterministically (random seed 42) into train/validation/test with proportions 70%/15%/15% = 420/90/90. Labels are programmatically derived from emulator ground truth: 'supported' if emulator-state implies no issue for the asserted property, 'unsupported' otherwise. No human annotation is used. If a scenario produces multiple distinct assertions in one LLM response, extract assertions deterministically (rule-based parser) and treat each extracted assertion as a separate sample; overall planned sample count remains 600 samples (300 scenarios × 2 prompts) after parser checks and deterministic re-run exclusion rules described in preregistration.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: compute precision, recall, F1 for judge and baseline on the held-out test set (n=90). 95% CIs via bootstrap with 1000 resamples stratified by class. Compare judge vs baseline with McNemar's test on paired binary decisions (alpha=0.05). Report confusion matrices and per-signal ablations (remove retrieval evidence, remove telemetry, remove validator) trained and evaluated with identical splits and seeds. Provide calibration plots and Brier scores. Perform deterministic sensitivity analyses: (1) exclude samples with missing retrieval/telemetry, (2) impute missing evidence scores as zero. All code and seeds are published; analysis is reproducible with CPU-only scikit-learn pipelines.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory metric is judge F1 on test split. Secondary analyses (precision, recall, calibration, ablations) are exploratory but reported with two-sided 95% CIs. For multiple hypothesis testing across ablations and subgroups, control false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05. Declare the primary outcome result irrespective of secondary correction.
missingness_plan: Sources of missingness: failed retrieval (index unavailable), telemetry gaps from emulator runs, or parser extraction failures. Deterministic handling: (1) if retrieval/index build fails for a sample, set retrieval evidence scores to zero and flag sample for sensitivity analysis; (2) if telemetry is missing for a sample (emulator run failure), exclude the scenario and re-run deterministic emulator retry policy up to 2 times; if still failing, record as excluded and replace by the next scenario in the scripted scenario seed list to maintain n=300 scenarios. Exclusion rules, imputation, and final counts are documented and deterministic; sensitivity analyses report performance with and without imputed/missing samples.

benchmark_names: Synthetic NetOps Reachability/Health Emulator Suite (scripted for this study)
risk_factors: Index/retrieval corpus drift between index-build and evaluation runs
Non-deterministic LLM API nondeterminism affecting paired comparisons
Leakage from training-time or public knowledge causing LLM to memorize scenario specifics (external to simulation)
detection_procedures: Record and hash retrieval index and snapshot manifests (file-hash); detect changes by comparing hashes before evaluation.
For each LLM call, log full API response metadata, including nondeterminism seeds where provided; detect unusually high variance across paired reruns (diagnostic only).
Compare retrieval top-k snippet IDs against snapshot manifest; flag any snippet missing from snapshot as contaminated.
item_flagging_rules: If index-hash differs from preregistered snapshot, automatically flag all affected samples and exclude from primary analysis; instead include them in a predefined sensitivity cohort.
If emulator run failed and was replaced via deterministic replacement policy, flag resulting sample and report replacement count.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes flagged contaminated samples; report sensitivity analysis results including flagged items. All exclusions and flags are deterministic and recorded in execution logs.
residual_uncertainty: Residual risk that hosted LLM internal nondeterminism changes absolute outputs across time (paired design mitigates but does not eliminate).
Residual gap between synthetic/emulator telemetry and production telemetry realism.

budget_scenarios.description: CPU-only conservative scenario to conserve hosted-model calls: single hosted LLM instance, minimal retrieval top-k (k=5), single classifier (logistic regression), no ensemble ablations during primary run.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Estimated 1000 model calls covers 600 primary prompts + 300 validation/ablation calls (retrieval-guided prompts) within hosted_model_api limits; classifier training and analysis are CPU-only. This scenario reduces exploratory ablations to fit a tight model-call budget.

budget_scenarios.description: Balanced scenario preserving planned verification and designed ablations: single hosted LLM, retrieval top-k=10, perform ablation runs for each major signal (3 ablations), and full bootstrap CIs.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Matches the selected candidate's estimated_model_calls (1500). Calculation: 600 primary LLM prompts (600 calls) + ~300 retrieval-augmented re-prompts/top-k lookups counted as distinct API calls (~300) + 3 ablation runs over validation/test slices (~300) + 300 diagnostic/paired-check calls (logs/paired reruns) = 1500 planned calls. CPU-only training and analysis fit capability_manifest constraints.

budget_scenarios.description: Higher-cost scenario for exhaustive ablations and extra paired reruns: retrieval top-k=20, ensemble judge variants, and expanded bootstrap (2000 resamples).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Larger number of model calls to enable repeated paired reruns and higher top-k retrieval; within maximum_planned_model_calls (10000) but longer wall-clock. Recommended only if wall-clock/time budgets permit.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Judge F1 on binary supported vs unsupported labels (test set n=90).
power_plan.target_effect: Detect an improvement in F1 of 0.08 over baseline (e.g., baseline F1=0.68 → target F1=0.76) on test split.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Assertion sample (extracted assertion from an LLM response); samples are assumed independent across scripted scenarios.
power_plan.calculation_method: Precision of F1 estimated with bootstrap (1000 resamples). Power evaluated informally: with test n=90 and expected class prevalence ~40% unsupported, bootstrap CI width for F1 is expected ≲0.08 under conservative variance estimates. Paired McNemar's test used for confirmatory difference in binary decisions; given discordant-pair rates typical in similar mitigation studies, n=90 for test provides reasonable sensitivity to moderate effect sizes. Formal power curves produced via simulation using recorded variance from validation split (preregistered).
assumptions: Unsupported class prevalence ~40% in the generated dataset (derived from scripted scenario distribution).
Independence between sampled assertions after deterministic extraction.
Bootstrap (1000 resamples) approximates sampling distribution for CIs.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=90 and assumed variance, detectable F1 difference (two-sided) is approximately 0.07–0.10 at 80% power depending on class prevalence; exact MDE will be reported after validation-split variance estimation.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute CIs and McNemar test using combined validation+test (n=180) if discordant-pair counts are low.
Report results after excluding samples flagged for missing retrieval/telemetry.
Simulate reduced unsupported-class prevalence (down to 25%) to show robustness of primary outcome.

transformation_families: Prompt-template variations (two canonical templates and minor deterministic paraphrases)
Retrieval embedding and top-k scoring (deterministic index build and cosine-similarity scoring)
Feature extraction from telemetry (windowed statistics) and validator outputs (binary+explanatory flags)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Deterministic re-run of prompt-template paraphrases on 10% audit sample; require identical ground-truth labeling after parser extraction for equivalence.
Recompute retrieval top-k ranks with seed-fixed index build; require same top-1 snippet ID on audit sample.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject a sample (exclude from primary analysis) automatically if parser extraction fails deterministically after two automatic re-executions.
Reject samples if index-hash mismatch is detected against preregistered snapshot.
Reject scenario if emulator run fails after two deterministic retries and replace with next seeded scenario to preserve total counts.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: 10% of all samples (random seed 2026) are re-executed deterministically end-to-end (indexing, retrieval, LLM prompt, parser) and hashes compared; any discrepancy triggers automated exclusion and is recorded. Audit logs and re-execution manifests are published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Feature mapping code (published) includes assertive unit tests ensuring consistent column order, types, and null-handling. Feature extraction is deterministic and runs with fixed seeds.
residual_risks: Differences between synthetic telemetry and production telemetry remain; transformation validation cannot eliminate this external-validity gap.
Hosted LLM internal nondeterminism may vary outputs even with identical prompts; paired comparisons mitigate but do not fully remove this risk.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Generalisability of results from synthetic/emulator telemetry to real production telemetry and vendor diversity.
Potential overfitting of the classifier-based judge to artifacts of the scripted scenario corpus despite deterministic sampling and ablation.
Latencies and operational costs of retrieval+validation pipeline in live deployments (not evaluated here; out of scope).
Hosted LLM internal nondeterminism could increase variance of absolute LLM baseline performance; paired design reduces but does not eliminate this issue.
